title: Improving the TENOR of Labeling: Re-evaluating Topic Models for Content Analysis
task: Evaluating topic models by how well they help people build label sets
problem: Coherence-based evaluation may not reflect how useful topic models are for real content analysis.
architecture: TENOR: topic models combined with an active-learning classifier in an annotation interface; simulated labelling experiments, a 60-person user study (15 per group) on Bills and an expert pilot; label sets scored against gold labels with purity, ARI and adjusted NMI.
key_results: BERTopic has the highest NPMI (0.15 on Bills, 0.10 on 20newsgroup) and ETM the second highest, yet in simulated labelling CTM is best and ETM worst.
LDA and sLDA are better than or competitive with ETM and BERTopic in the labelling task; CTM is also best in the user study.
strengths: Ties evaluation to a realistic content-analysis workflow with real users and experts.

limitations.text: Focuses on one narrow task; English data only.
